title: Home Mortgage Loans: when mortgage insurance applies, automatic PMI termination and how long FHA MIP lasts
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: when mortgage insurance applies, automatic PMI termination and how long FHA MIP lasts

This policy governs mortgage insurance on Home Mortgage Loans: when private mortgage insurance (PMI) applies, when it ends without any request, how long FHA mortgage insurance premium (MIP) is paid, and what happens to the escrow payment once insurance is removed.

## Policy clauses

1. **When PMI applies.** PMI applies to the programs that set a PMI threshold, when the loan's original loan-to-value ratio exceeded that threshold.
2. **Automatic PMI termination.** PMI terminates automatically, without a request, on the date the scheduled balance reaches the program's automatic termination level of the original value, if the loan is current on that date; otherwise on the first day of the month after the loan becomes current.
3. **FHA MIP.** FHA MIP ends after the program's MIP year count only when the original loan-to-value ratio was 90 percent or less; otherwise it lasts for the life of the loan.
4. **VA loans.** VA loans carry no monthly insurance.
5. **Effect on the payment.** Removing insurance lowers the monthly escrow payment by the premium, from the next installment.

## Automatic termination: branch table (hypothetical dates)

| Loan on the date the scheduled balance reaches the level | Date PMI terminates |
|---|---|
| Current | That same date |
| Not current; becomes current on 17 August | 1 September, the first day of the month after it becomes current |
| Not current; becomes current on 1 March | 1 April, the first day of the month after it becomes current |

## FHA MIP duration (hypothetical original ratios)

| Original loan-to-value ratio | MIP lasts |
|---|---|
| 88.00 percent | Until the end of the program's MIP year count |
| 90.00 percent | Until the end of the program's MIP year count, as 90 percent is "90 percent or less" |
| 90.01 percent | For the life of the loan |

## Points of judgement

- **Is a borrower request needed for automatic termination?** No. It happens without a request.
- **Which balance is used for automatic termination?** The scheduled balance, compared with the original value.
- **When does the lower escrow payment start?** From the next installment after the insurance is removed.
- **Hypothetical case.** A loan whose monthly escrow payment includes a mortgage insurance premium of 95.00 has its insurance removed; from the next installment its monthly escrow payment is 95.00 lower.
